answer: We formalize a protocol where agents must commit dynamic opportunity-cost bonds into a staking pool, ensuring that each attempt to wander from consensus triggers a subgame-perfect punishment matrix. This mechanism prevents an adversary from finding a meadow of profitable Sybil multiplication, as cumulative slashing penalties force a loss spiral that yields strictly negative expected utility. Consequently, the system converges to a robust Nash equilibrium where the incremental expense of identity proliferation dominates any potential gain.
